targets.authors: Lopez, M., Whalley, J., Robbins, P., & Lister, R.
targets.title: Relationships between reading, tracing and writing skills in introductory programming
targets.evidence_quote: We performed a quantitative, conceptual replication of Lopez et al. (2008)’s program­ ming skill hierarchy using a large, non-major introductory Python course.
targets.outcome_quote: With respect to RQ1, the hierarchy between Sequence, Tracing, Explaining, and Writing programming skills does not replicate with structural equation modeling as one of the candidate “best” models. However, the original hierarchy is still within the top 10 BIC scores for exam 2 and notably similar hierarchies appear in the “best” models for exam 1 and 3. The answer to the research question, then, is that our results do not support the specific hierarchy proposed by Lopez et al. (2008) as the strongest hierarchy.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit answer to RQ1 says the specific original hierarchy does not replicate and is not supported as strongest. Similar neighboring models are not confirmation of that central claim. Limitations of deriving teaching order from correlations do not erase this reported replication comparison. Other cited studies are background.
